stories.body: Russian ballistic missile strikes hit the Boryspil district east of Kyiv early Saturday, killing at least three people, including a child, and wounding three others, Ukrainian officials said. Explosions were heard across the capital, where falling debris damaged apartments and cars and fires broke out at buildings, garages, a business and a fuel tank. The attack highlights Ukraine's increasingly strained air defences: officials say supplies of interceptor missiles have fallen sharply, while Patriot systems remain the country's only reliable means of stopping ballistic missiles. The strikes came as Ukraine continued attacks on Russian oil refineries and logistics targets, and as the US Senate approved a sanctions package aimed at Russian energy exports.
stories.headline: Russian strikes near Kyiv kill three people, including a child

stories.body: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement, a mutual-defence pact declaring that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack on all of them. The agreement, signed in Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, does not specify what military action the countries would be required to take. The partners said it builds on longstanding strategic and defence cooperation and is intended to strengthen collective security amid escalating regional tensions linked to the US-Israel war on Iran, attacks involving Iranian-aligned groups, and broader concerns over regional stability.
stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sign mutual defence pact

stories.body: Right-wing lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president in Cali after defeating the left's candidate in June's runoff, pledging a hard-line campaign against armed groups and drug trafficking. De la Espriella said peace talks with criminal and rebel groups were exhausted, promised to cut state spending by up to 40 percent, revive the oil and gas sector and use aerial herbicides against coca crops. The Trump administration said it intends to provide $1 billion in security assistance, subject to work with Congress, as part of a renewed partnership. De la Espriella also plans to join the US-backed Shield of the Americas anti-drug initiative, restore ties with Israel and sever relations with Cuba and Nicaragua.
stories.headline: Colombia's new president Abelardo de la Espriella takes office as US pledges $1 billion in security aid

stories.body: A 14-year-old student shot and killed his grandparents before opening fire at Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, northwest of Bangkok, killing five teachers and later taking his own life, police said. A student subsequently died of injuries, bringing the death toll to eight, while more than 20 other people were wounded, several critically. Police said the teenager used his grandfather's legally registered gun, firing at least 26 rounds, but no motive has been established. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he would pursue new restrictions on carrying firearms in public, though he did not set out whether the measures would also tighten gun-ownership rules.
stories.headline: Thailand school shooting leaves eight dead, including the suspected teenage attacker

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 4,000 confirmed cases and 1,800 deaths, prompting Africa's public-health agency to expand its response and send community health workers door to door to search for patients. Officials are concerned that the unusually severe Bundibugyo-strain outbreak could involve viral mutation and plan studies with the World Health Organization. More than two-thirds of deaths have occurred outside treatment centres, while many patients were not previously identified as contacts, indicating extensive untracked transmission. The outbreak, centred in conflict-affected Ituri province, has spread to several other provinces and briefly crossed into Uganda.
stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo surpasses 4,000 cases

stories.body: A federal appeals court upheld an injunction stopping above-ground construction of President Donald Trump's $400 million White House ballroom, ruling that Congress must authorize such a fundamental redesign of the executive residence. The 2-1 decision backed a lower-court order obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation after the administration demolished the East Wing to begin the project. The majority said presidents are temporary tenants of the White House rather than its owners, and that the executive branch had not shown Congress delegated authority for the work. The ruling is stayed for 14 days to allow an appeal to the Supreme Court; Trump said he would immediately seek one.
stories.headline: US appeals court halts construction of Trump's White House ballroom

stories.body: The US Senate voted 86-11 to pass the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, a sanctions package aimed at reducing Russian energy revenues that finance the war in Ukraine. The bill would authorize tariffs of up to 100 percent on countries importing Russian oil and gas and target maritime networks used to evade Western embargoes. It now goes to the House of Representatives, which is not expected to vote before early September because of the congressional recess. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen welcomed the vote, while some House Democrats raised concerns that the tariff authority could be used too broadly by President Donald Trump.
stories.headline: Senate passes sanctions bill targeting Russian and Iranian energy

stories.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $567 million and impose new protections for young Facebook and Instagram users after finding that the company created a public nuisance that endangered children. The order includes a 90-hour monthly usage limit for users under 18, restrictions on AI chatbots, required warnings and stronger age-verification measures, although the requirements apply only in New Mexico and no deadline has been set for their implementation. The penalty follows $375 million in civil penalties awarded by a jury in March. Meta said it would appeal and maintained that it has worked to protect teenagers online.
stories.headline: Court orders new child-safety safeguards for Meta after major New Mexico ruling

stories.body: Wildfires are reaching communities beyond areas traditionally considered at high risk in the US West, while firefighting operations in Utah and Oregon have turned deadly. In Oregon, 47-year-old bulldozer operator Jason Ensign was killed after the fast-growing Wrights Spring Fire cut off his escape route near Chiloquin. In central Utah, a heavy-lift Sikorsky S-64 firefighting helicopter crashed while working the Widemouth 2 Fire near Richfield, with the condition of its two occupants initially unknown because crews could not safely reach the site. Hot, dry conditions, erratic winds and dry thunderstorms have complicated fire suppression across the region.
stories.headline: Wildfires spread beyond familiar risk zones in the US West as firefighting incidents turn deadly

stories.body: Spain will impose temporary identity, nationality and, where relevant, visa or residency checks on travellers arriving from Italy by air and sea from midnight on August 8 until September 7. Madrid announced the reciprocal measure after Italy refused to end checks it had imposed on arrivals from Spain following the mass crossing into Ceuta from Morocco at the end of July. Spain called Rome's action discriminatory and unjustified, arguing that onward migration from Spain to Italy is negligible and that most of the approximately 72,000 people who entered Ceuta have returned to Morocco. Italy said it would retain its controls until at least August 15, citing security, terrorism and migration concerns.
stories.headline: Spain introduces border checks for travellers from Italy amid the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Aid groups and authorities in Ceuta are warning of acute risks to migrant women and children following last week's mass arrival from Morocco, including homelessness, sexual violence, trafficking and forced return. Health sources have confirmed four alleged rapes of girls and six complaints in total, while local associations say resources and safe accommodation are inadequate. Spain's public prosecutor has issued instructions to ensure protection for unaccompanied foreign minors and said prosecutors will act if regional governments refuse or delay receiving children relocated from Ceuta. The youth minister said 1,342 children had been registered in the reception system and that transfers to the mainland could begin within weeks.
stories.headline: Ceuta migration crisis raises alarms over deaths and protection of children and women

stories.body: Authorities ordered residents of Sierra Engarcerán in Castellón to remain indoors after smoke from a wildfire that began in Vall d'Alba threatened the area. The regional emergency service issued an Es-Alert telling people to close doors, windows and ventilation systems, switch off air conditioning and extractors, while some rural homes were evacuated as a precaution. Firefighters, forest brigades, water tenders and the Military Emergency Unit were deployed. The blaze was among several vegetation fires in the Castellón interior, where thunderstorms, lightning, hail and strong winds have complicated operations; separate major fires in Niebla, Huelva, also prompted evacuations and military assistance.
stories.headline: Wildfires trigger evacuations and confinement alerts in Castellón

stories.body: Spain is expected to experience broadly dry, sunny and exceptionally hot weather during the total solar eclipse on August 12, although low cloud and afternoon storms could hinder viewing in some areas. Forecasters say temperatures may reach 40C in the middle Ebro valley and exceed 35C in many other locations along the path of totality. Afternoon storms remain possible in northeastern and southeastern mountain areas, while cloud is also possible in northern Galicia and Asturias. Meteorologists say low and layered clouds pose the greatest threat to direct observation, though even under cloud cover people should notice the progressive darkening and unusual grey light as totality approaches.
stories.headline: Spain prepares for the August 12 total solar eclipse amid heat and cloud concerns

stories.body: CCOO has called an indefinite strike by Barcelona's on-foot AREA parking inspectors every Saturday from August 8 through January 16, 2027, affecting enforcement in blue and green parking zones. The union is seeking repayment of wage deductions imposed during an earlier strike over Sunday and holiday work, after a court found the changes to working conditions unjustified and ordered previous schedules restored. Vehicle and motorcycle patrol staff will continue working, so parking violations can still be fined, and other unions have not joined the action. Municipal operator BSM says the strike is disproportionate and argues that its new 2026-29 collective agreement resolved the long-running dispute with majority backing.
stories.headline: Barcelona parking-zone inspectors begin an indefinite Saturday strike

stories.body: Rail infrastructure manager Adif will resume compaction work in Barcelona's Trinitat Vella next week with additional monitoring and measures intended to reduce vibrations, after about 80 residents were evacuated early Thursday. Firefighters found no structural damage and residents were allowed to return, but the work was halted for inspections. The project, linked to the Vallbona rail bypass, will continue for about four weeks only on weekdays and during daytime hours, with Adif promising to improve the compaction method, notify residents of potentially disruptive activity and install more topographic sensors and seismographs. Neighbours remain concerned because several nearby 70-year-old buildings are in poor condition and affected by aluminosis.
stories.headline: Adif will resume Trinitat Vella rail works with new safeguards after vibrations forced evacuations

stories.body: Residents of the 31 flats and ground-floor business at 54 Sant Gervasi de Cassoles, one of eight buildings evacuated after the L9 metro works sinkhole in Barcelona's Putxet neighbourhood, will have to wait until next week to return. The Catalan government delayed the planned return to carry out additional technical checks, though it expects residents of around 60 percent of affected homes to be back over the coming week. Monitoring and ground-consolidation work continues, including intensified injections and inspections around a separate building on Rubinstein Street where a new cavity and cracks were found. Officials say results show general stabilisation, while 50 affected people have received emergency expense advances and more have sought rent-payment suspensions.
stories.headline: Return of residents to another building evacuated after the L9 sinkhole is delayed

stories.body: Severe thunderstorms brought intense rain, hail and strong winds to northern Catalonia, prompting red weather warnings in areas including Berguedà and Vallès Oriental and activating the Inuncat flood-emergency plan. Hail and heavy rain affected the Cerdanya, Ripollès, Osona and Garrotxa, briefly closing the Bracons tunnel and interrupting the R3 commuter rail line between Ribes de Freser and Planoles after a tree fell. Forecasters also expect very intense heat for the August 12 solar eclipse, with temperatures near 40C in Lleida and around 33C in Barcelona. Conditions should generally be stable, but residual high and middle clouds from possible Pyrenees storms could obstruct the low western horizon during the eclipse.
stories.headline: Catalonia faces intense heat and severe storms in the north ahead of next week's eclipse
